extraction.name: Science Question Answering (SCIENCE QA)
extraction.description: SCIENCE QA is a new benchmark that consists of 21,208 multimodal multiple choice questions with diverse science topics and annotations of their answers with corresponding lectures and explanations. It is a large-scale multi-choice dataset that contains multimodal science questions with explanations and features rich domain diversity, collected from elementary and high school science curricula.
extraction.creator: Pan Lu, Swaroop Mishra, Tony Xia, Liang Qiu, Kai-Wei Chang, Song-Chun Zhu, Oyvind Tafjord, Peter Clark, Ashwin Kalyan
extraction.citeAs: Pan Lu, Swaroop Mishra, Tony Xia, Liang Qiu, Kai-Wei Chang, Song-Chun Zhu, Oyvind Tafjord, Peter Clark, Ashwin Kalyan. Leam to Explain: Multimodal Reasoning via Thought Chains for Science Question Answering. 36th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2022). arXiv:2209.09513v2 [cs.CL] 17 Oct 2022.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Questions in the SCIENCE QA dataset are sourced from open resources managed by IXL Learning, an online learning platform curated by experts in the field of K-12 education. The dataset includes problems that align with California Common Core Content Standards. To construct SCIENCE QA, the original science problems were downloaded and individual components (e.g. questions, hints, images, options, answers, lectures, and solutions) were extracted based on heuristic rules. Invalid questions, such as questions that have only one choice, questions that contain faulty data, and questions that are duplicated, were manually removed. If there were multiple correct answers, only one correct answer was kept. Answer options of each question were shuffled to ensure choices do not follow any specific pattern. Semi-automated scripts were used to reformat the lectures and solutions. A data exploration tool was developed to review examples, and incorrect annotations were further manually revised by experts.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Document analysis, Manual Human Curator, Software Collection
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: For questions without any context (7,188 or 33.9% of questions), the context text is replaced with an empty string.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Questions in the SCIENCE QA dataset are sourced from open resources managed by IXL Learning, an online learning platform curated by experts in the field of K-12 education.
extraction.rai:dataImputationProtocol: For questions without any context, the context text is replaced with an empty string.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Invalid questions (e.g., only one choice, faulty data, duplicates) were manually removed. If multiple correct answers applied, only one was kept. Answer options were shuffled. Semi-automated scripts were used to reformat lectures and solutions.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Invalid questions (e.g., only one choice, faulty data, duplicates) were manually removed. If multiple correct answers applied, only one was kept. Answer options were shuffled. Semi-automated scripts were used to reformat lectures and solutions.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Most questions are annotated with grounded lectures and detailed explanations. The lecture provides general knowledge that introduces background information for solving problems of a similar class. The explanation reveals a specific reason for the answer. Incorrect annotations were further manually revised by experts.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: A data exploration tool was developed to review examples in the collected dataset, and incorrect annotations were further manually revised by experts.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: A captioning model based on ViT and GPT-2 (tool2 from huggingface.co/nlpconnect/vit-gpt2-image-captioning) was used to generate captions for images in the dataset.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The collected data does not contain personally identifiable information or offensive content. The dataset does not contain any user usage data or personally sensitive information such as gender and race.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The SCIENCE QA dataset is proposed to diagnose the multimodal understanding and multi-hop reasoning abilities of AI systems. It adheres to the goal of AI for the common good, with any anti-social data points to be removed based on feedback. The dataset and methods are beneficial for follow-up research in multi-modal learning, multi-hop reasoning, and general artificial intelligence. It will contribute to the development of K-12 education applications such as tutoring systems and investigates the ability of large language models to mimic human thought processes.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: After careful examination of our dataset, to our best knowledge, we have not found any improper content, such as pornographic information, racial remarks, or harmful social bias.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation, Fine Tuning. The dataset serves as a new benchmark for multimodal multiple choice science questions, suitable for multi-modal question answering and multi-hop reasoning for AI systems. Its goal is to aid the development of reliable models capable of generating coherent chains of thought to reveal multi-step reasoning processes. It provides a useful benchmark for multi-modal learning, multi-hop reasoning, and general artificial intelligence, and can contribute to K-12 education applications like tutoring systems.
